I might revise this again later, but here are some of my preliminary thoughts:

[General]

- Players with no prior knowledge may find the following confusing:
1) the definition of a codon; it is missing from your description
2) how the 5' cap and poly-A tail affect the mRNA
3) how/when mRNA sequences "exist" and/or "terminates properly"

- To be very precise, mRNA encodes for the production of polypeptides, which then fold into proteins 😉

[Title]

- Please change DNA to mRNA.

[Goal]

- I agree with @5DN1L that the table might be too cumbersome to read during a clash, and that it's probably ok to omit it altogether.

- Consider this sample paragraph:
"A messenger RNA (mRNA) is a sequence of nucleotides ({{A}}, {{C}}, {{G}}, and {{U}}). Your cells use mRNA to build <<amino acid>> chains by reading groups of {{3}} nucleotides called <<codons>>, from <<left to right>>, as follows:

• The mRNA is first scanned for the <<start codon>> {{AUG}}.
• If found, the mRNA is translated <<codon by codon>>, beginning with the start codon. Each codon encodes for a specific amino acid, and these amino acids are chained together in the same order as their codons.
• Translation stops when one of the <<stop codons>> ({{UAG}}, {{UAA}}, {{UGA}}) is translated, even if there are more nucleotides left in the mRNA sequence. This termination forms a proper amino acid chain that is later folded into proteins.

Given an mRNA sequence:
• If no start codon exists, output {{NONE}}.
• Else, if no stop codon exists, output {{ELIMINATE}} (abnormal translation).
• Else, output its proper amino acid sequence after translation.

<<Example>>
```mRNA:  AGUCGAUGGUGAGUUGACUAAUGAA
codon:      |_||_||_||_|
          AUG GUG AGU UGA
amino:    Met Val Ser STOP```

You may reference it to craft your own paragraph; however, please include points (1) and (3) (from "General") in your paragraph.

[Input]

- Please format "codon:amino acid" as "[[codon]]{{:}}[[amino acid]]".

- Consider removing the 5' cap and (optionally) the poly-A tail from your input strings.

- For your consideration: consider limiting the full set of 20 amino acids to just a smaller subset of ~5-8, along with their corresponding codons. This might make it easier for players to interpret and handle; for example, you could list them out in the problem description and have the players decide how to handle / hardcode the translation.

[Constraints]

- Please state that each [[codon]] is a sequence of exactly {{3}} nucleotides ({{A}}, {{C}}, {{G}}, and {{U}}).

- Please state that each [[amino acid]] is either {{STOP}} or a {{3}}-letter sequence (e.g. "Met", "Phe", etc.)

- Please state that [[s]] will only contain the 4 listed nucleotides ({{A}}, {{C}}, {{G}}, and {{U}}), apart from the 5' cap and poly-A tail.

[Cases]

- Please add some cases where there are multiple start codons (AUG). These start codons could appear before or after the intended stop codon.

Thank you! :)

I'll review your clash in detail later today, but for the time being, I'd point out that the table may be too wide to display properly. Also, since it's already included in the input, I don't think it needs to be repeated in the Goal section.

Instead, I'd recommend showing just the beginning of the list from Input line 1, e.g. "UUU:Phe UUC:Phe UUA:Leu UUG:Leu UCU:Ser…" in the Goal section as a brief illustration of what the input looks like. Then, you could follow that with an illustrated example of a small test case. Showing how to read the full table (row/column) doesn't really help much with solving the task 😉
Any and all help with this would be appreciated!

Yeah, I figured. I originally wanted to only have one line of input, that being the mRNA sequence, but I thought it was too hard so I added the table to the input as well. I'll get those changes done now.

Thank you so much for all of these amendments!!!

I decided against touching the input as I don't think the 5' Cap changes anything, even if nobody understands it, and removing the Poly-A Tail also changes nothing for the most part.

Also, limiting the amount of amino acids is a great idea and would allow me to put a table back in the statement and remove it from the input; however, this is just personal preference, I like having them all as it's more "realistic".

Thank you so much for all the amazing changes, though! My statement was an absolute mess XD

Stub generator / Input / Constraints
* Consider revising Line 1 of the stub generator to:
loopline 64 codonCombination:word(8)

* After the above change,

  • Line 1 could be revised to include a reference to [[codonCombination]].

  • The first constraint could be revised to:
7 ≤ length of [[codonCombination]] ≤ 8

Input
* Consider adding "prefix" (or with brackets, i.e. "(prefix)") after "5' Cap".

* Please format "m7Gppp" and "AAAA" as {{constants}}.

Cases
* These cases are the same:
  • Eliminate (Test 4)
  • Eliminate (Test 5)

  Please revise them so that they're different. Also, is one case pair intended to cover the "Eliminate" scenario, and the other pair the "No Stop Codon" scenario? Please rename and/or regroup Pair 4 and Pair 5 as necessary.

* Start Codon After Stop Validator (Validator 8): [[s]] doesn't end with a Poly-A tail.

* While all codons have been covered at least once in the validators, some (including the stop codon UAG) have never been covered in any tests. Please revise the tests to ensure full codon coverage.

Thanks.

Thank you so much for the feedback! I believe I just corrected everything, except for the stub generator / input / constraints because I didn't really understand it. Could you explain what you have in mind by, "include a reference to [[codonCombination]]"? Once again, thanks for the help!

I meant the variable name [[codonCombination]] could be included in the description. A possible revised description of Line 1 is: "A string consisting of all 64 space-separated [[codonCombination]]s, each in the format of [[codon]]{{:}}[[amino_acid]], representing a codon and the amino acid it codes for."

Hope this clarifies!
I just changed it accordingly. Is it good now?

Thank you for the update. There are a couple of additional adjustments:

Stub generator
* Please change 10000 to 1000 to match the upper bound of [[s]] stated in the Constraints section.

Constraints
* Please remove the first constraint.

Cases
* Please modify the cases so that the lengths of [[s]] in each test and its corresponding validator are similar (within ±10%). The current mismatches are:

  • Test 1 (length = 67) vs Validator 1 (length = 223)

  • Test 2 (length = 403) vs Validator 2 (length = 223)

  • Test 4 (length = 630) vs Validator 4 (length = 999)

  • Test 8 (length = 36) vs Validator 8 (length = 999)

  • Test 9 (length = 42) vs Validator 8 (length = 931)

* Please also try to smooth out the progression of input lengths across the case pairs. For example, aim for a length of around 20 in Pair 1, around 50 in Pair 2, and so on, with the lengths increasing gradually.

* Please order the case pairs by increasing input length so that the cases with the longest inputs appear at the end.
I have made a few changes. The current tests and validators aren't great so I'll be changing them later; however, could you please comment on the lengths and the organization of them?

Thank you for the changes.

Cases
* The length similarity now looks good.

* For the organisation, it's about grouping the case pairs by scenario in a logical way, while also increasing input lengths and smoothing out their progression across the pairs. For example, something along the lines of 20, 50, 100, 150, and so on, depending on how many case pairs you have.

* You've already got a good variety of scenarios covered in the case pairs. The only additional scenario I'd like to see is a normal sequence beginning immediately after "m7Gppp". There are currently inputs of this form, but they're the "ELIMINATE" cases.

Constraints
* Please group the constraints on [[s]] together and put both of them at the end. In general, the constraints should follow the order in which the inputs are introduced.

For your reference, here are two others points I checked that you've already covered with the existing cases:

* Index of start codon (AUG) mod 3: 0, 1 and 2 are all present.

* Stop codons: The substrings UAG, UAA and UGA all appear in a normal sequence, but they belong to consecutive codons rather than functioning as actual stop codons.
I believe I have completed everything. How is it now?
Sorry, correcting myself: Instead of "if no stop codon exists", I think it would be more correct to say "if no stop codon was translated".

Everything else looks good; the only thing that's still a bit off is the input length progression. How about modifying the cases like this:

* Stop Codon Before Start Long (Pair 9): Reduce the input length to around 100.

* Start Codon After Stop Long (Pair 11): Reduce the input length to around 200.

* Largest (Pair 12): Reduce the input length to around 300.

* Normal 2 / Check Every Codon 2 (Pair 2): Move this pair to the end.

After that, change 1000 to 500 in both the Constraints section and the stub generator.

Thanks.
I changed a little bit, but I don't want to take away the length of 1000 as the last one. I think it's a good test case with good coverage. How are the others now, though?

Overall, the progression is slightly better than before. It's still not ideal, but I'm not going to suggest any further changes at this point. For future contributions, though, please remember to balance coverage across the possible input values and ranges, and to smooth out progression as much as possible.
